glosses: door bejegening met ruwe woorden van zich afschrikken

examples.text: Hij had me niet moeten afblaffen dat is belachelijk, wat er dan ook is gebeurd, je hebt dat niet op anderen af te reageren.

translations.source_sense_description: door bejegening met ruwe woorden van zich afschrikken

glosses: losfahren, ein Fahrzeug starten, zu fahren beginnen

examples.text: Ich versuchte anzufahren, aber der Motor streikte.

glosses: heranfahren, näher kommen

examples.text: Er ist mit lautem Trara angefahren gekommen.

glosses: ein Ziel beim Fahren haben, einen Ort anzielen

examples.text: Zu Mittag habe ich dann München angefahren.

glosses: eine Ware mit einem Fahrzeug herbei karren

examples.text: Im Herbst hatten wir genug Kohle für den Winter angefahren.

glosses: zusammenstoßen, zusammenfahren, mit einem Fahrzeug kollidieren

examples.text: Laut Polizeibericht hat er an der Kreuzung den Fußgänger angefahren.

glosses: laut zurechtweisen

examples.text: Der Lehrer hat in der Pause den Schüler laut angefahren.

glosses: eine Produktion starten, eine größere Maschinerie starten

examples.text: Der Hochofen wurde erst nach den Feiertagen wieder angefahren.

glosses: eine Lagerstätte erschließen

examples.text: Nächste Woche werden die Grubenleute die nächsttiefere Schichte anfahren.

translations.source_sense_description: door bejegening met ruwe woorden van zich afschrikken

glosses: mit groben Worten laut zurechtweisen

examples.text: Kam der Schiffsjunge dagegen aus Süddeutschland und verstand er nicht einmal die plattdeutschen Wörter, mit denen die Steuerleute ihre Befehle brüllten und die Matrosen ihn anschnauzten, dann konnte er sich auf reichlich Schläge einstellen.
Ich schnauzte nie jemanden an, weil ich das unhöflich finde.
Es ist nicht gut, die Kinder immer gleich anzuschnauzen.
Der eben angeschnauzte Junge duckte sich und verschwand.

translations.source_sense_description: door bejegening met ruwe woorden van zich afschrikken

glosses: To entangle; to complicate; to involve in knots.

examples.text: to snarl a skein of thread
And from her backe her garments she did teare, / And from her head oft rent her snarled heare[…]

glosses: To become entangled.
To place in an embarrassing situation; to ensnare; to make overly complicated.

examples.text:
November 9, 1550, Hugh Latimer, Sermon Preached at Stanford
[the] question that they would have snarled him with

glosses: To be congested in traffic, or to make traffic congested.
To form raised work upon the outer surface of (thin metal ware) by the repercussion of a snarling iron upon the inner surface; to repoussé
A knot or complication of hair, thread, or the like, difficult to disentangle.
An intricate complication; a problematic difficulty; a knotty or tangled situation.
A slow-moving traffic jam.

examples.text: The biggest cities feel the most acute impact of the last mile – of the squads of trucks and vans, the parcel hubs and sorting centres, the parking snarls and the discarded boxes.

glosses: To growl angrily by gnashing or baring the teeth; to gnarl; to utter grumbling sounds.
To complain angrily; to utter growlingly.
To speak crossly; to talk in rude, surly terms.

examples.text: It is malicious and unmanly to snarl at the little lapses of a pen, from which Virgil himself stands not exempted.

glosses: The act of snarling; a growl; a surly or peevish expression; an angry contention.
A growl, for example that of an angry or surly dog, or similar; grumbling sounds.
A squabble.

translations.source_sense_description: door bejegening met ruwe woorden van zich afschrikken

glosses: To slight, ignore or behave coldly toward someone.

examples.text: When, therefore, the First Secretary sounded him as to the expediency of some step in the direction of a firmer political combination than that at present existing,—by which of course was meant the dethronement of the present Prime Minister,—Mr. Roby had snubbed him!
For near three mortal months have you trifled with my feelings, eluded me, and snubbed me; and I won’t stand it!

Lily was sure that within twenty-four hours the story of her visiting her dress-maker at the Benedick would be in active circulation among Mr. Rosedale’s acquaintances. The worst of it was that she had always snubbed and ignored him.

For a long time he lived in the toy cupboard or on the nursery floor, and no one thought very much about him. He was naturally shy, and being only made of velveteen, some of the more expensive toys quite snubbed him.

glosses: To turn down insultingly; to dismiss.

examples.text: He snubbed my offer of help.
The joke is on those who snub books which, judged by their covers, are written for the mass market. Mineshaft is the finest satire in gay literature.

glosses: To check; to reprimand.
To stub out (a cigarette etc).
To halt the movement of a rope etc by turning it about a cleat or bollard etc; to secure a vessel in this manner.
To clip or break off the end of; to check or stunt the growth of.
Conspicuously short.

examples.text: a snub-nosed revolver

glosses: Flat and broad, with the end slightly turned up.

examples.text: It was even less easy to fix the impression in the case of the man at the right end of the table, who, to say truth, was as commonplace a person as could be seen anywhere, with a round, brown-haired head and a round snub nose, but also clad in clerical black, of a stricter cut.
If I close my eyes I can see Marie today as I saw her then. Round, rosy face, snub nose, dark hair piled up in a chignon.

glosses: Derived from a simpler polyhedron by the addition of extra triangular faces.
A deliberate affront or slight.

examples.text: It was part of Evelyn’s character that in spite of many snubs which she received or imagined, she never gave up the pursuit of people she wanted to know, and in the long run generally succeeded in knowing them and even in making them like her.
I hope the people we couldn't invite don't see it as a snub.

The bluntness of King Vajiralongkorn's intervention—and the determination it reveals to resist relatively small checks on royal power—is both a snub to the junta and a worry for democrats, some of whom had dared hope that the new king might be happy to take a back seat in public life.

The snub from a traditional ally to Putin, who had hosted an inconsequential meeting of the warring countries’ leaders last month, comes immediately on the back of his disastrous summit with six former Soviet states.

glosses: A sudden checking of a cable or rope.
A knot; a protuberance; a snag.

examples.text: [A club] with ragged snubs and knotty grain.

glosses: To sob with convulsions.

examples.text: He striveth, strugleth, roareth, sobbeth, snubbeth, and ready he is to burst for anger.
